analyst_view.overall: Early view: Eibar are fourth but have not played since a 1-1 draw with Almería on 31 October, after their trip to Castellón was postponed, and have one league win in their last five after a club-record winning streak. Cádiz are 20th and have lost two in a row under Borja Jiménez, who replaced Albert Celades in late October, per one report; they also lost Javi Castro to injury at home to Oviedo.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar are described as the side with the least ball in the division and win by keeping games tight, and four of the last five meetings ended 1-0 to one side. Cádiz have scored only once in each of their last two league games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, with 5.4 for Eibar. I lean slightly lower: a side that plays with little of the ball rarely builds the sustained pressure that wins corners, even at home, and Cádiz under Jiménez only pushed forward after half-time changes in their last game.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean higher: Aranbarri has publicly asked his players to recover the aggressiveness they lacked, and a Cádiz side in the relegation zone, beaten twice in a row, will have to fight for every second ball. Cádiz at 3.4 looks plausible; Eibar at 1.9 looks low.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 17.5 for Eibar. That looks high for a team that plays with so little of the ball; I expect Eibar to take fewer, better chances and Cádiz to get around ten. Two weeks without a league game adds to the case for a slower match.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the goals and shots: Eibar scored one goal or none in each of their last three league games, and Cádiz have been blunt away from home (one goal at Mallorca, none at Granada).
